info.title: EMotorad warranty API
info.description:
## How to use this page

For the Amiigo app team. The sections follow the rider through the app in the order of the Figma file ([Amiigo Grooming File, page "Full flow - Amiigo"](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File)):

0. Sign in (Go auth service) and 0b. My bikes (Go bike service): the Go backend, not this service. Each of their calls names its own server.

Home: the first warranty call after sign-in, `getHome`, every Home card the warranty service owns in one answer (and the cycle nickname).

1. Find your cycle, 2. Upload invoice, 3. Register or claim, 4. My cycles and warranty, 5. Choose a plan and pay, 6. My plan, 7. Free service QR: the warranty API.

Open a section, then a call. Every call of the app starts with the same block: **Screen** (the Figma frames, linked), **When** (the tap that makes the call), **Send** (what the screen supplies), **Use in the screen** (which response field fills which part of the screen), **Next** (the next call or screen for each answer) and **Errors to handle here** (every code the call can answer and what to show). The schemas and examples follow. Each call also carries `x-figma`, the frame names and node ids, for tools.

The sections after 7 are called by other systems (the OMS, the AI support bot, the Go backend, the web backend, Razorpay, the load balancer). The app never calls them.

Screens that call no API on this page: the Razorpay checkout (the provider SDK), the plan terms (static), frame scanning (the camera), "Skip registration" and "Exit reminder".

## The token handover

The warranty API never signs a rider in. The Go auth-server does (section **0. Sign in (Go auth service)**), and its access token is the warranty API's `riderToken`:

1. `sendOtp` with the phone answers `token`. In Authorize, paste it as `goOtpToken`.
2. `verifyOtp` with the same phone and the code answers `access_token` and `refresh_token`. Paste the refresh token as `goRefreshToken`.
3. No role call is needed (staging since 6 Oct 2026): verify's access token already works on the warranty API, even on the very first sign-in of a phone. `setUserRole` only changes the role.
4. Paste verify's access token as `riderToken` (without the word Bearer). Every warranty call of sections 1 to 7 takes it, and so do `setUserRole`, `logout` and the bike routes.
5. When a call answers that the token expired (warranty `401 TOKEN_EXPIRED`, Go `401 expired token`), `refreshSession` with the refresh token answers a new access token: paste it again. Before the access token has expired it answers 429 instead.

Locally, use only mock phones (`+919000000003` to `+919000000100`, code 1234) and the local Go auth-server, the first server of each section 0 call when this page is served locally. Its tokens are signed with the same throwaway key the local warranty server checks, so the handover works end to end (`docs/api/README.md`).

Every app call of sections 1 to 7 needs the rider token (Authorize, `riderToken`). Every call that changes something takes a fresh `Idempotency-Key` per tap, reused only to retry that same tap. Amounts are minor units (paise).

The screen guide, with a flow diagram per journey and the known gaps: `docs/api/screens.md` in the em-platform repo ([open it](./screens.md) from the static page). Tokens, idempotency, rate limits and the error envelope: `docs/api/app-contract.md`. Staging, step by step (hosts, test numbers, sign-in, Try it out against staging): `docs/api/staging-quickstart.md` ([open it](./staging-quickstart.md) from the static page).

## For the AI chat service

The chat service never signs a rider in either. The app hands it the rider access token, and:

1. **Who the rider is:** verify the token with the Go public key, [`listPublicKeys`](#/Go%20auth%20service%20public%20keys%2C%20not%20called%20by%20the%20app/listPublicKeys) (PASETO v4.public; cache the keys, refetch on an unknown key id). Its payload carries `emuserId` (the account) and `phone`. No API call is needed for the phone.
2. **The rider's cycles, model and warranty status, by phone, server to server:** [`searchRegistrationsByPhone`](#/AI%20support%20bot%2C%20not%20called%20by%20the%20app/searchRegistrationsByPhone) with the AI service key (Authorize, `serviceKey`). Each item has `frameNumber`, `productName`, `purchaseDate`, `status` (`active` or `pending_review`) and `coverage` (per part, with `validUntil`). No personal fields.
3. **Or the same with the rider's own token:** [`listMyRegistrations`](#/4.%20My%20cycles%20and%20warranty/listMyRegistrations).
4. **Assure or Assure+ plan of a cycle:** [`getPlanSubscriptionForRegistration`](#/6.%20My%20plan/getPlanSubscriptionForRegistration) with the rider token and the `registrationId`.

## About this document
Rider, service-caller and provider-webhook HTTP API of the warranty service: registration, Assure plans and payments. Every route lists its error codes in `x-error-codes`. Generated from the real Fastify route registrations by service/scripts/write-openapi.ts -- never hand-edited.

riderToken.description: A PASETO v4.public access token for a signed-in rider, issued by the Go auth service (ADR 0013): the `access_token` of `verifyOtp`, `setUserRole` or `refreshSession` in section 0. This service only verifies it. The same token goes to the warranty calls (sections 1 to 7) and to the Go routes that take an access token. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

serviceKey.name: x-service-key
serviceKey.description: A raw shared secret for one of the four known callers (oms, ai, web, go), hashed with SHA-256 and compared against the configured hash for each (ADR 0015). The service infers the caller from which hash matches; the header carries only the secret itself, no name.

webhookSignature.name: x-razorpay-signature
webhookSignature.description: An HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with the provider webhook secret, in hex. It is the only credential of the webhook route: no bearer token, no service key.

partnerWebhookSignature.name: x-partner-signature
partnerWebhookSignature.description: An HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with the partner key's own webhook secret, in hex. It is the only credential of the insurance partner webhook: no bearer token, no service key.

goOtpToken.description: The `token` that `POST /v1/otp/send` (section 0) answers: a PASETO v4.public token of type `otp` for that one phone, valid for the OTP lifetime (`OTP_DURATION`). Only `POST /v1/otp/verify` takes it. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

goRefreshToken.description: The `refresh_token` that `POST /v1/otp/verify` (or `POST /v1/social/verify`, or a rotating `POST /v1/session`) answers: a PASETO v4.public token of type `refresh`. Only `POST /v1/session` takes it. Keep it in secure storage; never send it to the warranty API.

post.summary: Send the sign-in code to a phone
post.description:
**Screen:** [Empty](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (Phone sign in, in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Select country](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (Phone sign in, in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Number entered](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (Phone sign in, in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Invalid number](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (Phone sign in, in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Code resent](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding")

**When:** The rider taps Continue on "Number entered" (Phone sign in), and again on Resend code on "Enter verification code" ("Code resent").

**Send:** 
- `phone` (body): the country picked on "Select country" plus the number field, as E.164 (`+919000000042`). Check the length in the app first: "Invalid number".

**Use in the screen:** 
- `token`: nothing on screen: keep it in memory for `verifyOtp` (its `Authorization` header).

**Next:** 
- Success: "Enter verification code". Next call: `verifyOtp`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `400` `field: Phone, expected e164`: "Invalid number" (Phone sign in). The app should catch this before the call.
- `400` `field: Phone, expected required`: a client bug: `phone` is missing.
- `430` `unable to send sms`: "We could not send the code, try again". The SMS provider refused or did not answer.
- `500` `database error`: "Something went wrong, try again". Redis or Postgres failed.
- `500` `internal error`: "Something went wrong, try again" (the OTP token could not be made).
- Every Go route answers errors as `{"error": true, "message": "..."}` with the status above and no error code: tell the cases apart by status, and by `message` where one status has several. A body that is not valid JSON answers 400 with the Go JSON decoder's own text (for example `unexpected EOF`, or `EOF` for an empty body), and a second JSON value after the first answers 400 `body must only have a single JSON value`. Several missing or invalid fields answer one 400 whose message joins the `field: ..., expected ...` parts with ", ". All of these are client bugs: fix the request.

**Known gap, for Sachin to decide:** 
- No send limit and no attempt counter on this branch (a2-rollout.md: Task 11 is on `fix/auth-hardening`). Production also accepts the fixed code 1234 for about 2,600 mock numbers until Task 10 ships.

**Live in production today:** yes, on `origin/amigo-prod-deployment` (auth-server). Unchanged on A2.

post.summary: Check the code and sign the rider in
post.description:
**Screen:** [Enter verification code](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Verification code entered](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Verifying code](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Incorrect verification code](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding")

**When:** The rider types the fourth digit on "Enter verification code" ("Verification code entered"); "Verifying code" shows while the call runs.

**Send:** 
- `Authorization` (header): `Bearer <token>`, the `token` of `sendOtp` (Authorize box `goOtpToken`).
- `phone` (body): the phone sent to `sendOtp`, unchanged.
- `otp` (body): the four digits, as a number.
- `device_id` (body): a stable id of this install (optional; new on A2).
- `link_token` (body): only after `verifySocialSignIn` answered `link_required` (new on A2).

**Use in the screen:** 
- `access_token`: store it: the `riderToken` of the warranty calls (sections 1 to 7) and of `setUserRole`, `logout` and the bike routes.
- `refresh_token`: store it securely, for `refreshSession`.
- `new_user`: true: the profile and role screens next; false: Home.
- `bike_vin`: the connected bike to pair with, when not empty.
- `default_saved`: whether the rider saved a default role before.
- `isUserNew`: true: an account created since 6 Oct 2026 (every sign-in); false or missing: an older account.

**Next:** 
- signed in (`new_user` true or false): Enter frame number or Home. The warranty journey starts at section 1 with this access token. No role call is needed: the new app has no role screen and a new account is `EM_USER` by default. Next call: `lookupFrame`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `419` `invalid otp`: "Incorrect verification code". The rider may type again; no new send needed.
- `429` `expired otp`: not a rate limit: no code could be read for this phone (expired, already used, never sent, or Redis could not be read). "Code expired", offer Resend code (`sendOtp`). A mock phone never gets it: its code is fixed.
- `401` `invalid token`: no OTP token, a token that is not an OTP token, or `phone` is not the phone the code was sent to: back to Phone sign in.
- `401` `expired token`: the OTP token expired: "Code expired", Resend code (`sendOtp`).
- `400` `field: Phone, expected e164`: a client bug: send the phone exactly as sent to `sendOtp`.
- `400` `field: Phone, expected required`: a client bug: `phone` is missing.
- `400` `field: Otp, expected required`: a client bug: `otp` is missing or 0.
- `400` `json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field verifyOtpRequest.otp of type int`: a client bug: `otp` must be a JSON number, not a string.
- `500` `database error`: "Something went wrong, try again".
- `500` `internal error`: "Something went wrong, try again" (the sign-in event could not be sent, or a token could not be made).
- Every Go route answers errors as `{"error": true, "message": "..."}` with the status above and no error code: tell the cases apart by status, and by `message` where one status has several. A body that is not valid JSON answers 400 with the Go JSON decoder's own text (for example `unexpected EOF`, or `EOF` for an empty body), and a second JSON value after the first answers 400 `body must only have a single JSON value`. Several missing or invalid fields answer one 400 whose message joins the `field: ..., expected ...` parts with ", ". All of these are client bugs: fix the request.

**Known gap, for Sachin to decide:** 
- Fixed on staging on 6 Oct 2026 (backend `feat/a2-auth` `582d8d1f`): the first sign-in of a phone now gets the same tokens as every later one, level 1 with the phone, so its access token works on the warranty API at once and no `setUserRole` call is needed. A new account keeps the default role `EM_USER`. Production still runs the code before A2, where the first sign-in's tokens carry level 0 and no phone and `setUserRole` was the way round it.

**Live in production today:** yes, on `origin/amigo-prod-deployment` (auth-server). New on A2, both optional and ignored when absent: `device_id` (a per-device session, Task 15) and `link_token` (finish a social sign-in, Task 23). The response is unchanged.

patch.summary: Save the rider's role and get a fresh access token
patch.description:
**Screen:** [Verifying code](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding")

**When:** Right after `verifyOtp` answered `new_user` true, once the rider has picked a role; the Figma Onboarding section has no role screen, so this runs behind "Verifying code" or the profile screens that follow it.

**Send:** 
- `Authorization` (header): `Bearer <access_token>` of `verifyOtp` (Authorize box `riderToken`).
- `user_role` (body): the role the rider picked (2 for an Amigo rider).
- `device_id` (body): the same value as on `verifyOtp` (new on A2).

**Use in the screen:** 
- `access_token`: store it in place of the old one: from now on it is the `riderToken`.
- `user_role`: the saved role.

**Next:** 
- Success: Home, then the warranty journey from section 1 with this token. Next call: `lookupFrame`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `401` `invalid token`: no `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, or a token this service cannot verify. Sign in again (section 0).
- `401` `expired token`: the token has expired. For an access token, refresh (`refreshSession`), then retry once.
- `403` `unauthorized`: the bearer token is not an access token (the refresh token was sent): a client bug.
- `500` `internal error`: the body does not decode for this route (not JSON, empty, `user_role` as a string, `emuserid` not a UUID), or the role event could not be sent, or the token could not be made. Fix the request; otherwise retry.
- `500` `database error`: "Something went wrong, try again". Also a `user_role` outside 0 to 3 (a client bug).
- `401` `invalid token`: also, with `SESSION_REQUIRED_FOR_ACCESS` on only: this device's session was revoked (it logged out). Sign in again.
- Every Go route answers errors as `{"error": true, "message": "..."}` with the status above and no error code: tell the cases apart by status, and by `message` where one status has several.

**Known gap, for Sachin to decide:** 
- The Figma Onboarding section shows no role screen, and the new app does not need this call: since 6 Oct 2026 (staging) the first sign-in already gets a full token, and a new account is `EM_USER` by default. Call it only to change the role.

**Live in production today:** yes, on `origin/amigo-prod-deployment` (auth-server). New on A2: optional `device_id`, read only when `SESSION_REQUIRED_FOR_ACCESS` is on (Task 18). With the flag off (the default) the route behaves exactly as on production.

**Flag:** `SESSION_REQUIRED_FOR_ACCESS`. Off by default. On: a device whose session was revoked (it logged out) is refused with 401 `invalid token`; a rider with no session row at all is still allowed.

post.summary: Get a new access token with the refresh token
post.description:
**Screen:** [Splash](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding")

**When:** On "Splash" when the stored access token has expired, and whenever a call answers that the access token expired (Go 401 `expired token`, warranty 401 `TOKEN_EXPIRED`). Never before the access token has expired: an early refresh answers 429.

**Send:** 
- `Authorization` (header): `Bearer <refresh_token>` (Authorize box `goRefreshToken`).
- `phone` (body): the signed-in rider's phone.
- `device_id` (body): the same value as on `verifyOtp` (new on A2).

**Use in the screen:** 
- `access_token`: store it: the new `riderToken`. Retry the call that failed.
- `refresh_token`: only when present (rotation on): store it in place of the old.

**Next:** 
- Success: retry the call that answered expired, once, with the new token.
- 409, 420, or 401 on this call: the session is over: sign in again from "Welcome · Sign in options". Next call: `sendOtp`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `429` `too many requests`: refreshed again before the access-token lifetime (`ACCESS_TOKEN_DURATION`) passed since the last sign-in or refresh. Keep using the current access token; no error on screen. A refresh refused with 401 for a wrong `phone` also restarts that window (the Go code records the attempt before it checks the phone).
- `409` `Multiple Login`: this refresh token is no longer the account's current one (signed in again on another device, or logged out): sign in again.
- `420` `session expired (something fishy may be happening)`: rotation on only: an already used refresh token came back, so the session was ended. Sign in again.
- `401` `invalid token`: not a refresh token, a token this service cannot verify, or `phone` is not the account's phone: sign in again.
- `401` `expired token`: the refresh token itself expired (`REFRESH_TOKEN_DURATION`): sign in again.
- `400` `field: Phone, expected e164`: a client bug: send the E.164 phone.
- `400` `field: Phone, expected required`: a client bug: `phone` is missing.
- `500` `database error`: "Something went wrong, try again".
- `500` `internal error`: "Something went wrong, try again" (a token could not be made).
- Every Go route answers errors as `{"error": true, "message": "..."}` with the status above and no error code: tell the cases apart by status, and by `message` where one status has several. A body that is not valid JSON answers 400 with the Go JSON decoder's own text (for example `unexpected EOF`, or `EOF` for an empty body), and a second JSON value after the first answers 400 `body must only have a single JSON value`. Several missing or invalid fields answer one 400 whose message joins the `field: ..., expected ...` parts with ", ". All of these are client bugs: fix the request.

**Live in production today:** yes, on `origin/amigo-prod-deployment` (auth-server). New on A2: optional `device_id`, and with `REFRESH_ROTATION_ENABLED` on a rotated `refresh_token` in the answer and the 420 reuse answer (Task 16). Flag off (the default): the answer is `{"access_token": ...}` exactly as on production.

**Flag:** `REFRESH_ROTATION_ENABLED`. Off by default: the account's single refresh token decides, and no `refresh_token` comes back. On: the per-device session decides and the refresh token rotates; the app must then store every new `refresh_token` (a2-rollout.md row 5: an app release first).

post.summary: Sign the rider out on this device
post.description:
**Screen:** no frame in the Figma source: Log out sits in Profile, which the source does not list.

**When:** The rider taps Log out.

**Send:** 
- `Authorization` (header): `Bearer <access_token>` (Authorize box `riderToken`).
- `phone` (body): the signed-in rider's phone.
- `device_id` (body): the same value as on `verifyOtp` (new on A2).

**Use in the screen:** 
- `(body)`: nothing: `null`. Delete both stored tokens.

**Next:** 
- Success, or any error: delete both tokens and show "Welcome · Sign in options".

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `401` `invalid token`: no `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, or a token this service cannot verify. Sign in again (section 0).
- `401` `expired token`: the token has expired. For an access token, refresh (`refreshSession`), then retry once.
- `401` `invalid token`: also when `phone` is not the access token's phone. Delete the tokens anyway.
- `403` `unauthorized`: the bearer token is not an access token: a client bug.
- `500` `database error`: delete the tokens anyway.
- Every Go route answers errors as `{"error": true, "message": "..."}` with the status above and no error code: tell the cases apart by status, and by `message` where one status has several. A body that is not valid JSON answers 400 with the Go JSON decoder's own text (for example `unexpected EOF`, or `EOF` for an empty body), and a second JSON value after the first answers 400 `body must only have a single JSON value`. Several missing or invalid fields answer one 400 whose message joins the `field: ..., expected ...` parts with ", ". All of these are client bugs: fix the request.

**Live in production today:** yes, on `origin/amigo-prod-deployment` (auth-server). New on A2: optional `device_id`; the logout also ends that device's session row (Task 17). The legacy refresh token is invalidated as on production.

**Flag:** `REFRESH_ROTATION_ENABLED`. Off: the revoke of this device's session row is best effort; a failure to invalidate the refresh token still answers 500. On: the revoke and the invalidation are one transaction, and a failure of either answers 500.

post.summary: Sign in with Apple or Google (Firebase ID token) (new on A2)
post.description:
**Screen:** [Welcome · Sign in options](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Sign in · Apple](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Sign in · Google](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding")

**When:** The rider taps Apple or Google on "Welcome · Sign in options" and the Firebase SDK returns an ID token ("Sign in · Apple", "Sign in · Google").

**Send:** 
- `id_token` (body): the Firebase SDK's ID token.
- `device_id` (body): a stable id of this install (optional).

**Use in the screen:** 
- `status`: which way to go (see Next).
- `access_token`: `signed_in`: store it, the `riderToken`.
- `refresh_token`: `signed_in`: store it securely.
- `link_token`: `link_required`: keep it for `verifyOtp`; never show it.

**Next:** 
- `signed_in`: Home. Next call: `lookupFrame`.
- `link_required`: "Phone sign in": the rider proves the phone once; send the `link_token` with the code. Next call: `sendOtp`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `404` `404 page not found`: plain text, not JSON: social sign-in is off (`FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` unset). Hide the buttons.
- `401` `expired token`: the Firebase ID token expired: get a fresh one from the SDK and retry once.
- `401` `invalid token`: any other verification failure (signature, issuer, audience, provider, or a token used twice): "Sign-in failed, try another way".
- `429` `too many requests`: more than 20 tries in an hour from this address: "Try again later".
- `503` `service unavailable`: Firebase's keys could not be fetched, or the replay check could not reach Redis: "Try again shortly".
- `400` `field: IdToken, expected required`: a client bug: `id_token` is missing.
- `400` `field: IdToken, expected maxbytes: 4096`: a client bug: `id_token` is over 4096 bytes.
- `500` `database error`: "Something went wrong, try again".
- `500` `internal error`: "Something went wrong, try again" (the sign-in event could not be sent).
- Every Go route answers errors as `{"error": true, "message": "..."}` with the status above and no error code: tell the cases apart by status, and by `message` where one status has several. A body that is not valid JSON answers 400 with the Go JSON decoder's own text (for example `unexpected EOF`, or `EOF` for an empty body), and a second JSON value after the first answers 400 `body must only have a single JSON value`. Several missing or invalid fields answer one 400 whose message joins the `field: ..., expected ...` parts with ", ". All of these are client bugs: fix the request.

**Known gap, for Sachin to decide:** 
- No Firebase project and no per-brand app registration exist yet (a2-rollout.md, section 7); the Apple and Google frames have no working route anywhere until then.

**Live in production today:** no, new on `feat/a2-auth` (auth-server). New on A2 (Tasks 21 to 23). Not on production.

**Flag:** `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`. Unset (today, everywhere, and on the local run): the route is not mounted and answers 404 (text). Set: social sign-in works. No Firebase project exists yet.

post.summary: Add a bike to the rider's account by frame number (new on A2)
post.description:
**Screen:** no Figma frame yet: the multi-cycle switcher is A3 work and the design has no screen for it.

**When:** The rider adds another cycle to the account (the A3 multi-cycle switcher).

**Send:** 
- `Authorization` (header): `Bearer <access_token>` (Authorize box `riderToken`).
- `frame_number` (body): the typed or scanned frame number.
- `model` (body): the model the rider picked.
- `color` (body): the colour picked (optional).
- `nickname` (body): the name the rider gives it (optional).

**Use in the screen:** 
- `vin`: the bike to pair with over Bluetooth.
- `frame_number`: the frame on the bike card; the id of every later bike call.
- `primary`: whether this is now the bike shown first.
- `nickname`: the bike card title.

**Next:** 
- Success: the bike list. Next call: `listBikes`.
- The rider wants its warranty too: section 1, with the same frame number. Next call: `lookupFrame`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `404` `404 page not found`: plain text, not JSON, with a valid access token: `BIKES_V1_ENABLED` is off on this server (the default). Hide the multi-bike screens. Without a valid token the 401 below comes first.
- `401` `invalid token`: no `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, or a token this service cannot verify, or a token of the wrong type for this route. Sign in again (section 0).
- `401` `expired token`: the token has expired. For an access token, refresh (`refreshSession`), then retry once.
- `400` `field: FrameNumber, expected required`: inline error: enter the frame number.
- `400` `field: Model, expected required`: inline error: pick the model.
- `400` `frame number has invalid characters`: inline error on the frame number: only letters, digits and `-`.
- `422` `invalid frame number input`: inline error on the frame number: 9 to 17 characters.
- `400` `model does not exist`: a client bug: offer only the listed models.
- `400` `bike nickname must match the pattern: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, and special characters`: inline error on the nickname: letters, digits, spaces and `!@#$%^&*()+={}[]|\:;"'<>,.?/~` only (no `-` or `_`).
- `400` `bike colour may contain only letters, digits, spaces, - and _, up to 20 characters`: inline error on the colour.
- `427` `frame number already exists`: "This cycle is already on another account". Contact support.
- `409` `frame is registered to another rider`: only with `WARRANTY_LOOKUP_ENABLED` on: the warranty service says another rider holds this frame. "This cycle is registered to someone else".
- `427` `vin already paired`: "Something went wrong, try again" (a VIN clash even after one retry).
- `400` `invalid user`: the bike service has no row for this account yet: retry in a few seconds.
- `409` `bike change conflicted with another request, please retry`: two bike changes at once: retry the same call.
- `500` `database error`: "Something went wrong, try again".
- `500` `internal error`: either the bike was stored and its event failed (retry the same call: it finishes the job) or nothing was stored (the MQTT password could not be made): retry the same call.
- Every Go route answers errors as `{"error": true, "message": "..."}` with the status above and no error code: tell the cases apart by status, and by `message` where one status has several. A body that is not valid JSON answers 400 with the Go JSON decoder's own text (for example `unexpected EOF`, or `EOF` for an empty body), and a second JSON value after the first answers 400 `body must only have a single JSON value`. Several missing or invalid fields answer one 400 whose message joins the `field: ..., expected ...` parts with ", ". All of these are client bugs: fix the request.

**Known gap, for Sachin to decide:** 
- No Figma screen and no app spec for the multi-bike routes yet (a2-rollout.md: "App team spec for /v1/bikes", needed before A3).

**Live in production today:** no, new on `feat/a2-auth` (userbike-server). New on A2 (Tasks 29 to 31). Not on production; the app adds its first bike another way today.

**Flag:** `BIKES_V1_ENABLED`. Exactly `true` mounts the four `/v1/bikes` routes; otherwise they answer 404 (plain text) to a request with a valid access token, and 401 to one without (the token check of the whole `/v1` group runs first). Off by default; a2-rollout.md says to turn it on only after the hardening Tasks 1 and 10 and the warranty lookup (`WARRANTY_LOOKUP_ENABLED`).

post.description:
**Screen:** no Figma frame yet: the multi-cycle switcher is A3 work and the design has no screen for it.

**When:** The rider picks another bike as the main one in the switcher.

**Send:** 
- `Authorization` (header): `Bearer <access_token>` (Authorize box `riderToken`).
- `frame` (path): `frame_number` of the bike. No body.

**Use in the screen:** 
- `(body)`: nothing: `null`. Move the tick.

**Next:** 
- Success: refresh the list. Next call: `listBikes`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `404` `404 page not found`: plain text, not JSON, with a valid access token: `BIKES_V1_ENABLED` is off on this server (the default). Hide the multi-bike screens. Without a valid token the 401 below comes first.
- `401` `invalid token`: no `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, or a token this service cannot verify, or a token of the wrong type for this route. Sign in again (section 0).
- `401` `expired token`: the token has expired. For an access token, refresh (`refreshSession`), then retry once.
- `400` `frame number has invalid characters`: inline error on the frame number: only letters, digits and `-`.
- `404` `bike not owned by this account`: the frame is not one of this rider's bikes: refresh the list.
- `400` `invalid user`: the bike service has no row for this account yet: retry in a few seconds.
- `409` `bike change conflicted with another request, please retry`: two bike changes at once: retry the same call.
- `500` `database error`: "Something went wrong, try again".
- Every Go route answers errors as `{"error": true, "message": "..."}` with the status above and no error code: tell the cases apart by status, and by `message` where one status has several.

**Live in production today:** no, new on `feat/a2-auth` (userbike-server). New on A2 (Task 29). Not on production.

**Flag:** `BIKES_V1_ENABLED`. Exactly `true` mounts the four `/v1/bikes` routes; otherwise they answer 404 (plain text) to a request with a valid access token, and 401 to one without (the token check of the whole `/v1` group runs first). Off by default; a2-rollout.md says to turn it on only after the hardening Tasks 1 and 10 and the warranty lookup (`WARRANTY_LOOKUP_ENABLED`).

**When:** Home opens (after sign-in, and each time the rider comes back to it) and on pull to refresh. Load the AI support card in parallel from its own service; never wait on it.

**Send:** 
- `lat` (query): the phone's latitude, only when the rider allowed location; with `lng`, never one alone. Leave both out otherwise: there is then no nearest dealer.
- `lng` (query): the phone's longitude, with `lat`.

**Use in the screen:** 
- `rider.firstName`: "Hi <firstName>"; null: a greeting without a name.
- `rider.city`: the city under the greeting (and for the weather); null: none.
- `cycle`: null: the rider has no cycle registered yet; show "Register your warranty" (section 1).
- `cycle.nickname`: the cycle card title, with the pencil ("Naming cycle"). Never empty.
- `cycle.productName`: the model; null until the sale is verified.
- `cycle.frameNumber`: "Frame no." on the cycle card.
- `cycle.imageUrl`: the cycle image; null: the app's own picture.
- `cycle.status`: `pending_review` with `cycle.verification`: "Invoice not uploaded for warranty" or "checking your invoice".
- `warranty.kind`: `standard`, `assure` or `assure_plus`: picks the warranty card. `warranty.displayName` is its title.
- `warranty.status`: `active` is "Active"; `expired` is "Standard warranty expired"; `unknown` means no purchase date yet.
- `warranty.headline.validUntil`: "Valid till <date> on <parts>", the parts from `warranty.headline.parts` (motor and battery).
- `warranty.headline.monthsLeft`: "<n> months left"; the bar fills to `warranty.headline.progressPercent` (how much of the cover has run).
- `warranty.extend.eligible`: standard only: true shows "Extend my warranty" with "<warranty.extend.daysLeft> days left to extend". False: "Standard warranty with no extension".
- `warranty.planStatus`: `paused` is the "Payment missed" card (pay now in section 6).
- `services`: null: no services card. Shown only while an Assure or Assure+ plan is in force.
- `services.freeLeft`: "<freeLeft> of <services.total> free left, use by <services.useBy>".
- `services.nextClaimable.label`: "Claim service" is enabled while `services.nextClaimable` is not null.
- `dealer.sellingDealer.name`: the dealer card ("Dealer bought"): name, `city`, Call with `phone`.
- `dealer.nearestDealer.distanceKm`: "<name>, <city>, <distanceKm> km away", Navigate (`mapUrl`, else `latitude` and `longitude`) and Call (`phone`). Null: no dealer within 100 km, or no location sent.

**Next:** 
- The pencil on the cycle card: "Naming cycle"; save with the nickname. Next call: `setRegistrationNickname`.
- Extend my warranty: the plans of section 5, for `cycle.registrationId`. Next call: `createPlanQuote`.
- Claim service, or the warranty card of a plan: the plan screen with `services.subscriptionId` (or `warranty.subscriptionId`); each free service there shows its code and QR (section 7). Next call: `getPlanSubscription`.
- `cycle` null, Register: "Enter frame number". Next call: `lookupFrame`.
- The warranty card of a standard cycle: the Profile "Warranty" screen. Next call: `getMyRegistration`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `MARKET_DISABLED` (403): show Home without the warranty cards; no retry button.
- `TOKEN_INVALID` (401): the session is not valid: refresh the token with the Go auth service, retry once.
- `TOKEN_EXPIRED` (401): the session expired: refresh the token with the Go auth service, retry once.
- Any route can also answer `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400: a client bug, fix the request, do not retry), `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401: sign in again), `RATE_LIMITED` (429: back off for `Retry-After` seconds), and `INTERNAL` (500) or `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` (503): show the generic error with the `errorId` and retry later. See `docs/api/app-contract.md`.

**Screen:** [Standard · active](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=173-12488) (in "Warranty plan details post purchase (From Profile)"), [EX1 Standard warranty · expired](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=173-12488) (in "Warranty plan details post purchase (From Profile)"), [Warranty registered](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=25-15328), [Registered but unverified](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=599-64260) (the link lands near it)

**When:** The rider opens one cycle's warranty card; and as the poll after `createRegistration`, a `transferred` claim, or `submitRegistrationInvoice`.

**Send:** 
- `id` (path): the registration id.

**Use in the screen:** 
- `status`: `active` the cover screens; `pending_review` "Registered but unverified"; `cancelled` (a rejected create) or `superseded` (someone with stronger proof registered it).
- `verification.state`: `verifying` keep polling; `verified` done; `rejected` show `verification.code`.
- `verification.code`: why the invoice was rejected.
- `productName`: the cycle name on the cycle card.
- `productColor`: the colour on the cycle card.
- `frameNumber`: "Frame no." on the cycle card.
- `purchaseDate`: "Standard warranty Valid from <date>" and "Ran <date> – ...".
- `coverage.status`: for an `active` registration: `active` "Standard · active"; `expired` "EX1 Standard warranty · expired"; `unknown` no purchase date yet. A `pending_review` one always reads `unknown`: go by `status`.
- `coverage.components[].component`: each row of "Coverage breakdown" (Motor, Battery, Frame, Charger).
- `coverage.components[].months`: "1 year", "5 years", "6 months" per part.
- `coverage.components[].validUntil`: the end of each part; "Ended <date>" on EX1.
- `coverage.remedy`: `collect_purchase_proof` on an `active` registration: "add your purchase proof" and the invoice upload. A `pending_review` one carries it too: ignore it there.
- `coverage.extendedEligibleUntil`: a hint for "Buy extended warranty" or the "Boost" banner: the purchase date plus the default 30-day window. The quote's `eligibleUntil` is the real last day.

**Next:** 
- "Buy extended warranty" or Check now: "Assure+ selected". Next call: `createPlanQuote`.
- `status` `active`, `purchaseDate` null and `verification` null or `rejected` (not a `pending_review` registration): the invoice upload, then the late invoice. Next call: `submitRegistrationInvoice`.
- `status` `superseded`: "Someone with stronger proof registered this frame". No call.
- Polling and `verification.state` is still `verifying`: poll again (every 3 seconds for 60 seconds, then every 15). Next call: `getMyRegistration`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `MARKET_DISABLED` (403): "Not available in your region yet". No retry button.
- `REGISTRATION_NOT_FOUND` (404): "We could not find this cycle". Go back to the list or to lookup.
- `TOKEN_INVALID` (401): the session is not valid: refresh the token with the Go auth service, retry once.
- `TOKEN_EXPIRED` (401): the session expired: refresh the token with the Go auth service, retry once.
- Any route can also answer `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400: a client bug, fix the request, do not retry), `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401: sign in again), `RATE_LIMITED` (429: back off for `Retry-After` seconds), and `INTERNAL` (500) or `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` (503): show the generic error with the `errorId` and retry later. See `docs/api/app-contract.md`.

**Known gap, for Sachin to decide:** 
- No Figma frame shows an `active` registration with no purchase date (`purchaseDate` null, `coverage.status` `unknown`, `coverage.remedy` `collect_purchase_proof`) or the late invoice upload. Reuse the "Invoice upload" group until design adds one.

post.description:
**Screen:** [Enter frame number](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-4479) (the link lands near it), [Frame number entered](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Scan frame number](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Frame number already registered](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-4533), [Registered with dealer's number](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-4550)

**When:** The rider taps Next on "Enter frame number", with a typed or scanned frame number. Also from "Warranty not registered" > Register in Profile.

**Send:** 
- `frameNumber` (body): the frame number field, or the scanned value. The API takes 5 to 32 letters or digits once spaces, dashes and underscores are removed; real frames start N2, SK, E1, E4 or EM and run 9 to 22 characters, so never require an EM prefix.

**Use in the screen:** 
- `state`: picks the next screen (see Next).
- `data.registrationId`: keep it (`registered_to_you`, `registered_by_dealer`): the claim and every later call need it.
- `data.dealerName`: "Your dealer have registered this cycle earlier" (`registered_by_dealer`).
- `data.registeredOn`: when the dealer registered it (`registered_by_dealer`).
- `data.requiresInvoice`: `available` only: `true` means the invoice is needed; absent means the phone matched the sale.
- `data.productName`: the cycle name: `available` prefill (phone matched) and `registered_to_you`.
- `data.productColor`: the colour on the cycle card.
- `data.purchaseDate`: the purchase date, when known.
- `data.customerName`: `available` prefill only (phone matched): the buyer name on the sale, to prefill "Full name"; null when the sale has none. Never in any other state. No dealer name and no invoice number here: show `orderReference`.
- `data.postcodeRequired`: `available` and `not_found`: show a PIN field on the Name step only when true. Always true for `not_found` and `requiresInvoice`; on the prefill, true only when the sale has no PIN the registration can take.
- `data.coverage.components[].component`: the coverage breakdown on "Warranty registered" (`registered_to_you`).
- `data.status`: `registered_to_you` covers a pending registration too: `pending_review` is "Registered but unverified", `active` is "Warranty registered".
- `data.verification.state`: `registered_to_you`: `verifying` means the invoice is being read; poll the registration.

**Next:** 
- `registered_to_you` with `data.status` `pending_review`: "Registered but unverified"; poll while `data.verification.state` is `verifying`. Next call: `getMyRegistration`.
- `registered_to_you` with `data.status` `active` and `data.purchaseDate` null: no date yet: this lookup may have started reading a stored invoice, so read the registration first; if `verification` is null or `rejected`, offer the invoice upload and the late invoice (section 3). Next call: `getMyRegistration`.
- `registered_to_you` with `data.status` `active` and a `data.purchaseDate`: "Warranty registered" with the cycle and its cover. Check for a plan next. Next call: `getPlanSubscriptionForRegistration`.
- `registered_by_dealer`: "Registered with dealer's number", then the invoice upload, then the claim (section 3). Next call: `createDocument`.
- `registered_to_other`: "Frame number already registered": the rider checks the number or contacts support. No call.
- `available` with `data.requiresInvoice`: "Warranty registration" step 1, "Upload your invoice". Next call: `createDocument`.
- `available` without `requiresInvoice` (the phone matched the sale): skip the upload: step 2, the Name step, then the create without `documentId`. Next call: `createRegistration`.
- `not_found`: step 1, "Upload your invoice", then the create; it lands as "Registered but unverified". Next call: `createDocument`.

**Errors to handle here:** 
- `MARKET_DISABLED` (403): "Not available in your region yet". No retry button.
- `FRAME_SHAPE_UNKNOWN` (400): inline error on "Enter frame number": "Check the number". Figma has no frame for it; reuse the "Missing frame number" style.
- `LOOKUP_LIMIT` (429): "Too many tries, try again in a while". Same message as any 429.
- `TOKEN_INVALID` (401): the session is not valid: refresh the token with the Go auth service, retry once.
- `TOKEN_EXPIRED` (401): the session expired: refresh the token with the Go auth service, retry once.
- Any route can also answer `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400: a client bug, fix the request, do not retry), `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401: sign in again), `RATE_LIMITED` (429: back off for `Retry-After` seconds), and `INTERNAL` (500) or `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` (503): show the generic error with the `errorId` and retry later. See `docs/api/app-contract.md`.

**Known gap, for Sachin to decide:** 
- No Figma frame shows the prefill case: `available` without `requiresInvoice` (the phone matched the sale) can skip the upload and has `productName`, `productColor` and `purchaseDate` to show, but the design always asks for the invoice.

**Screen:** [Default](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (Invoice upload, in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Uploading](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-3481) (Invoice upload, in "EMO GO - Onboarding"), [Invoice Upload Required pop up Card](https://www.figma.com/design/D9vlE74upYFQsFD02CME46/Amiigo-Grooming-File?node-id=14-4839)

**When:** The rider picks a photo or PDF on "Upload your invoice" (Default), or taps Retry upload.

**Send:**

- `contentType` (body): the picked file's type: `application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png` or `image/heic`. Convert HEIC to JPEG first: this route takes it, but where invoice reading is on the create, the claim and the late invoice refuse it (`DOCUMENT_TYPE_NOT_READABLE`).

- `id`: the quote id for `acceptPlanQuote`.

- `priceSheet.tiers[].tier`: the tier key to send on accept.
- `priceSheet.tiers[].tierRank`: the order of the tabs and of "Compare plans".
- `priceSheet.tiers[].benefits[].label`: "What's Included" and "Compare plans" rows (+2 extra years motor, 3 Free Services...).
- `priceSheet.tiers[].benefits[].kind`: the icon of each row.
- `priceSheet.tiers[].benefits[].termMonths`: the length of a benefit, when it has one.
- `priceSheet.tiers[].couponValueMinor`: "Save ₹4,449 now" and the "₹4,449 off on your next cycle" row; null means no coupon.
- `priceSheet.tiers[].oneTimeTotal.grossMinor`: "One-time payment plan": "Pay Now ₹3,999" and "Proceed to pay ₹3,999".
- `priceSheet.tiers[].oneTimeTotal.taxMinor`: "incl. ₹719 taxes".
- `priceSheet.tiers[].monthly[].tenureMonths`: "Select Plan Tenure": 6, 12, 18, 24 months.
- `priceSheet.tiers[].monthly[].instalment.grossMinor`: "₹250/mo" per tenure and "Next month onwards ₹250/mo".
- `priceSheet.tiers[].monthly[].firstPayment.grossMinor`: "Pay Now ₹749" and "Proceed to pay ₹749" (first instalment plus upfront benefits).
- `priceSheet.tiers[].monthly[].firstPayment.taxMinor`: "incl. ₹138 taxes".
- `priceSheet.tiers[].upfront[].label`: the separate lines paid up front, for example "Theft Insurance".
- `priceSheet.tiers[].upfront[].grossMinor`: the amount of that line ("₹499").
- `priceSheet.tiers[].termsVersion`: send it on accept; never hard-code it.

- `currency`: the currency of every amount (amounts are minor units).

- `REGISTRATION_NOT_FOUND` (404): "We could not find this cycle". Go back to the list or to lookup.

post.description: **Not called by the app.** An insurance partner's signed answer to a policy request. Matched to the request by the partner's own request id (never across partners) and deduplicated by the partner's event id; `issued` stores the policy number, the dates and the policy document under `policies/` and moves the cover to `active`, `rejected` moves it to `policy_rejected` (shown in "Partner policies"). A policy is issued once: a later issued event for it changes nothing, the first number and document stay. A policy for a cover that was refunded or cancelled is stored and flagged, never activated. An event that matches no request is kept as `unmatched` and runs again when the partner sends it again. The signature goes in the `x-partner-signature` header (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body under that partner's secret), the `partnerWebhookSignature` box of Authorize. Answers 401 `PARTNER_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, 400 `PARTNER_WEBHOOK_INVALID`, 404 `PARTNER_NOT_FOUND`, and 413 above 256 KiB.

tags.name: OMS admin: plans, not called by the app
tags.description: Not called by the app. The plan catalogue admin: four OMS admin screens (Assure plans home, Draft editor, Publish dialog, Version history and compare) manage the Assure and Assure+ plans without a migration. OMS admin calls its own OMS, which checks the staff session and the `warranty_plans_admin` permission, then forwards here with service key `oms`, `X-Contract-Version` and the staff member as the actor (`X-Actor-Type` `staff`, `X-Actor-Id`); a call without a staff actor answers `ACTOR_REQUIRED`. The routes exist only while `PLANS_ADMIN_ENABLED` is true. Changes are `POST`, each with an `Idempotency-Key` (the preview takes none and never writes), because OMS admin only has GET and POST helpers. Publishing needs a reason and is audited; a published version never changes, and existing subscriptions and quotes in flight keep the prices they have.

tags.name: OMS admin: ops, not called by the app
tags.description: Not called by the app. The warranty ops screens of OMS admin: Warranty health, the exception lists, Subscription lookup and detail, Refunds, Partner policies and the Review queue. OMS admin calls its own OMS, which checks the staff session and the permission (`warranty_ops`, or `warranty_review` for the review detail), then forwards here with service key `oms`, `X-Contract-Version` and the staff member as the actor (`X-Actor-Type` `staff`, `X-Actor-Id`); every call goes through the OMS with the staff member as the actor, and a call without one answers `ACTOR_REQUIRED`. The routes exist only while `WARRANTY_HEALTH_ENABLED` is true (the partner routes: `PARTNER_POLICIES_ENABLED`; the review detail: `WARRANTY_REVIEW_DETAIL_ENABLED`); a route whose flag is off answers 404 `NOT_FOUND`. Every action takes a reason, an `Idempotency-Key` and writes an audit event. The support search is a `POST` so the frame number or phone never sits in a URL, and it is a read: it takes no `Idempotency-Key`. The Partner settlement screen reads the monthly statement partners are paid against (no money moves in the system); its three routes exist only while `PARTNER_SETTLEMENT_ENABLED` is true.

tags.name: stand-in payments (staging)
tags.description: Staging only, while STAGING_STAND_INS_ENABLED is true. The plans module runs the fake payment provider here: no money moves, there is no Razorpay screen, and every id is a fake one (`order_fake_`, `pay_fake_`, `sub_fake_`, checkout key `fake_key_razorpay`). To finish a purchase, the app calls one of these two routes in place of opening the Razorpay checkout, then the ordinary confirm route with the body it answers. One time: `acceptPlanQuote`, then `POST /api/warranty/dev/payments/capture` with `checkout.providerOrderId`, then `POST /api/warranty/v1/payments/{paymentId}/confirm`. Monthly: `acceptPlanQuote`, then `POST /api/warranty/dev/mandates/authorise` with `checkout.providerSubscriptionId`, then `POST /api/warranty/v1/payments/{paymentId}/confirm-mandate`. Pay now and upgrades work the same way. A rider token is required. The fake forgets its orders when the service restarts (each deploy): accept again after one. Never registered in production.
